en: The titan arum plant emits a foul odor resembling rotting meat to attract pollinating carrion beetles and flies.
Wombats produce cube-shaped feces to prevent the droppings from rolling away when marking their territory on rocks and logs.
The human stomach produces hydrochloric acid strong enough to dissolve zinc, but a thick mucus layer constantly protects the stomach lining from digesting itself.
The axolotl can regenerate its brain, heart, and limbs multiple times throughout its life without leaving any scar tissue.
Certain species of bamboo can grow up to 91 centimeters in a single day, making it the fastest-growing plant on Earth.
The wood frog survives harsh winters by completely freezing its body and stopping its heart, then thawing out alive in spring.
If you uncoiled all the DNA in a single human cell, it would stretch about two meters long.
An octopus has three hearts and blue blood, which efficiently pumps oxygen through its body in cold, deep ocean environments.
Rafflesia, a rare parasitic plant found in Philippine rainforests, lacks leaves, stems, and roots while producing the world's largest individual flower.
Adult mayflies live for only twenty-four hours because they lack functional mouthparts and stomachs, meaning they cannot eat during their brief reproductive stage.
A cubic inch of human bone can theoretically support up to five tons, making it stronger than steel of the same weight.
Parrotfish secrete a transparent mucus cocoon around themselves at night to mask their scent and protect against biting predators like moray eels.
